summary: This reference maps the installed Studio, Browser Studio, opt-in remote listeners and Kit. The public auditorium landing retains Mainstage's curtain film, Vaudeville title cards and 32 illustrated phrases before the feature pictures. The installed velvet landing retains its Dock, real scene data and capped light/fog behavior. Browser Studio reuses the React shell and canonical adapters with memory-only state, and includes the reviewed extension runtime with only Browser-declared operations. Kit owns providers, tools and staged review. Library, Workbench, Scenes, Press, Settings and shared components retain their existing owners. The rp-core wing renders all Director records in virtualized variable-height rows; Memory remains paged in groups of 20. Verification statements distinguish source, fixture, live-browser and packaged evidence. Launchers require an explicit matching product identity, return the actual bounded fallback port, and apply a twelve-second browser readiness deadline; native explicit ports remain isolated. Newly bound servers require an exact public instance ID independent of the session bearer. Native creation failure retains the owned server and uses the existing browser fallback instead of reporting a normal close. Normal downloads separate Windows, Linux and macOS apps from advanced source workflows. Published asset links share the release feed. Table Read adds bounded saved-model interviews, manually owned living fields, encrypted resume, offline review and exact-ID saves to ordinary characters.
topics: Context wing prompt inspector and memory

sections.title: Velvet premiere landing
sections.summary: Fresh launches use locally shipped stage artwork beneath live branding and navigation. Begin the showing runs the local curtain film, then the Vaudeville title cards and 32 illustrated Shakespeare phrases before the feature pictures; reduced motion skips the curtain and title sequence. Continue and Now Playing use real scene data. Quick Start routes to Library, import and Scenes. The Dock and shortcuts remain usable. A reusable proscenium frames scene artwork and HTML controls. Two capped OGL beams and fog suspend while hidden; Settings chooses Moving, Still or Off, and reduced motion makes Moving still. WebGL failure uses CSS fallbacks.

sections.title: Bottom app navigation
sections.summary: The bottom dock follows RoleCall geometry, with an accent glow and a collapsible edge pill. Every available discovered app appears; unavailable apps are excluded, with Settings and Overlay at the end. Tiles navigate the workspace. The dock sits above apps and below dialogs; its measured bottom reserve clears while hidden. Hidden controls remain inert and outside the tab order. Arrow keys, Home and End move focus. Theme slots remain decorative. Overlay and Ctrl+K or Cmd+K open the temporary overlay with theme and piece counts. The contextual status line holds real messages, failures and reload warnings, disappearing when empty. Narrow shells retain safe-area placement, 44px targets and the selected app in view. Coarse-pointer text focus hides the dock; physical-phone keyboard behavior is unverified. The packaged Linux app defaults to Studio and opens its verified address. Updates allow only same-platform old/new Linux x64 names and bound downloads to 512 MiB. Verified update files use shared atomic publication and owner-executable POSIX permissions.

sections.title: Browser Studio
sections.summary: GitHub Pages serves the public site at its root and Browser Studio under studio/. Browser Studio reuses the React shell, discovered apps, adapters, import/export and documentation with memory-backed data that lasts only for the page load. The reviewed extension runtime is available through Settings > Extensions; packages run in an isolated browser worker and receive only Browser-declared operations against the in-memory store. Provider calls, native file access and persisted rp-core scenes are not available to Browser extensions. This does not enable the standalone script test bench, which still requires the installed app. Export before reload. The public landing, tour pictures, Open Graph metadata, reduced-motion behavior and GitHub links are separate website content. The download page shows Windows, Linux and macOS choices, sharing the release-feed request. Only actual compatible latest-release assets become direct links; offline or missing states retain GitHub and source links. New public releases contain the Windows, Linux and macOS apps and checksums, while old recovery assets stay available.
topics: public website at the Pages root

sections.title: Kit terminal shell
sections.summary: Kit is a terminal shell with a multiline composer, paste cards, bounded follow-up queue, draft-preserving history and search, interruptible streaming, and argument-completing palette. Right-click pastes text; Alt+V attaches readable images or displays them without sending; paths in messages link only to those files. Native scrolling, foldable replies, copy feedback and stage watching support terminal use. Sessions resume, rewind, fork and export; model settings, doctor, inventory and privacy are commands. /rail keeps a preset block list beside conversation: ctrl+B focuses it, ctrl+shift+arrows resize, ctrl+shift+D changes density, and < or > pages presets. Rail content enters ambient context; Enter stages edits as one draft at the same Gate. Bounded tool reads replace model save prose with revision-checked REVIEW CHANGE; conversion uses REVIEW CROSSING. Held calls wait at the Gate and applies serialize. /privacy reports recorded model calls and token counts, not all network activity; the greeting discloses transmission to the selected provider and connected services.

sections.title: Hyper-modularity (the build's spine)
sections.summary: UI applications are drop-in folders exporting a BunzaiApp manifest and component. Bun discovery skips private underscore folders, bundles apps on demand, puts ordinary apps on the Dock, and keeps catalogOnly tools available through the catalog without a central roster. Apps receive AppContext and may reach engine or filesystem behavior only through its API; the shell owns global navigation, tabs, theme, and status. Visual law comes from one token sheet rather than app-local colors or fixed layout. Bright accents remain marks, borders, and spines; any labeled accent fill uses a generated deep companion with stage-white text. Rose, house accent, deck, and per-piece pairs share tested deepening logic.

sections.title: First-run setup (the wizard)
sections.summary: The wizard reuses the bunny-b app icon. First run is assembled from drop-in SetupStep folders that declare question, options, settings key, widget, stage treatment and recap; the wizard derives order, progress, defaults and summary from discovery. Settings are an open record parsed fail-closed per key and stored under the studio directory. Missing setupComplete opens the wizard; completion applies theme and house accent and the first landing, and later launches show the title screen and land on Scenes. Settings > Appearance offers host-verified bundled themes (Paper, GirliePop as stage, Theater) and approved data-only theme packages, with digest preview, disable, revoke, restore and remove; Encore ships uninstalled as an example. The saved theme is only a request: the shell paints the neutral core appearance until /api/themes/effective verifies it, and a local cache never activates one. Serialized PATCH writes merge concurrent changes. Boot paints the landing before the piece list; list loads retry after 2, 5 and 15 seconds, and a lasting failure leaves a sticky status note.

sections.title: The right-click system
sections.summary: One shared context-menu service grows through registration. Surfaces attach typed targets and data to elements, with the deepest matching element winning and a shell-level target always available. Features register any number of item providers for a target type; each provider contributes a section, an empty result denies by absence, and cleanup receives an unregister function. Shell providers currently cover entity actions such as send, show, open beside, split close, and Workbench removal, plus Dock-app and shell navigation actions. A new feature contributes one provider instead of editing a central switch, preserving room-independent behavior for common entity operations.

sections.title: Apps catalog and documentation
sections.summary: The Dock's Add app control discovers the manifest-marked catalog instead of naming an id, and the catalog derives cards from the running app roster. catalogOnly tools such as CSS Workshop and Help/Docs remain bundled without occupying everyday Dock space. Help/Docs reads the committed corpus through the generated docs index, which can merge frontmatter, semantic page summaries, retrieval topics, and nested section anchors. Navigation separates user workflows and platforms from developer API, architecture, data, format, security, extension, and decision material; ADR filenames remain canonical while titles are reader-friendly. Markdown uses the shared sanitizer, figures and images are restricted to generated or committed docs assets, the right rail follows current headings, and packaged content matches GitHub. External GitHub viewing passes through the leaving gate and URL allowlist. The catalog room is a room header over one framed card per app, marked On your Dock or Included app.

sections.title: Dev live-reload
sections.summary: Development Studio watches all of src (test files excluded) and broadcasts changes to every open page over the /dev/reload server-sent-event stream. Browser bundles are memoized and rebuilt only when the watcher sees an edit; the Browser shortcut serves production React while bun run dev keeps development React. Packaged executables serve baked assets, return 404 for the development stream, and let the client become quiet without a separate dependency.

sections.title: The card-type chip
sections.summary: Library summaries derive sourceFormat and sourceVariant from the first non-Bunzai escrow record. Labels come from the live format registry rather than a duplicated UI map: platform-specific adapters show platform and variant; generic Tavern/CC content shows CC plus the spec version on characters and no chip on other kinds, since CC means character card; pieces authored without a source adapter display no chip. The badge describes provenance without inventing one.

sections.title: The studio store
sections.summary: StudioStore is the Studio view of the encrypted library.db: versioned pieces with a 3-day Trash and retired deleted ids, and Studio documents in the StateStore. A plain folder is imported once; bunzai export writes it back. Calls answer 423 while locked. Saves never overwrite silently; inventory reports damaged rows. Inventory, list and graveyard read sealed summaries, not bodies, falling back to a body only when a summary is missing or stale. Full editor loads use the stored revision from the same stable read as hydrated art, so reopening uploaded pictures does not cause false save conflicts; concurrent changes still refuse writes. This path is HTTP-regression and live-browser proven.

sections.title: The receipt
sections.summary: The server renders one plain-language import receipt for both shells, ensuring terminal and visual users receive the same explanation. It uses recognizable platform names, a we-read/we-kept voice, and emits conditional lines only when engine evidence supports embedded books, scripts-as-data, or privileged warnings. Unknown files receive a warm failure message. Receipt rendering adds presentation, not new detection or format logic.

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.summary: The endpoint map covers authenticated Studio reads and writes, docs, staging, imports, scenes, agents and settings. Light reads retain sealed media references and expose targeted escrow and native metadata; patch saves require the opened revision and return committed identity. A stored Sprite pack prints as a zip through GET export-pack, one picture at a time, and duplicates by reference through POST duplicate, so a big pack never crosses the wire. Local staged uploads are bounded and inert; remote and LAN writes are refused. Asset GET and HEAD and pinned portrait routes compose with the same library lock lifetime. A dropped chat .jsonl rides the same inspect, save-bundle and save-staged routes: its row carries a scene carrier, never a library piece, and a refusal such as a card missing from the library answers ok false with 422 so the sheet lists it by file. Chat rows commit after cards and personas. Source-reviewed implementation and live proof are distinguished.
topics: pack zip export and duplicate by reference

sections.title: The Library room (the shelves - deep browse)
sections.summary: Library shows first-run doors when empty and, when populated, RoleCall's /library layout: a rail with RC's Carousel/Grid switch, deck rows with live counts, collections, and Add, folding into chips below 48rem of pane width. Each non-empty deck gets a numbered section of RC's cards; every section header switches its deck among Cards and the drop-in views. Cards carry the shelf tools; a New tile ends each row. The art dial defaults to 15.75rem-wide cards, search reaches tags, and ranges, Select all, and the agent walk one drawn order; layout, order, views, and size persist per user. Start Scene under a character card opens a new scene. Move to Trash keeps a piece 3 days, frees its name at once, and retires its id; the Trash panel holds deleted pieces, cut scenes, and deleted takes with the time left, and removed versions of replies marked kept until restored, filtered All, Pieces, or Scenes, and Restore brings each back whole.
topics: drop-in grid showcase and list views

sections.title: Scenes (the library's chats)
sections.summary: Scenes provides encrypted chats, frozen cast, takes, cuts and swipes. Full Chat and Messenger reuse wings. Control Booth applies loadouts with receipts and Undo; tracker state follows reply versions. Dramaturg keeps a separate sealed, revision-guarded conversation with six read-only tools. Runtime owns cancellation, shutdown and pre-egress limits; its four-scene, 32 MiB cache clears on lock/unmount and rejects stale responses. Deterministic-provider UI checks cover tools, reload persistence and floating panels. Narrow scenes use compact portraits and tap actions; the composer uses 16px text, a 5.5rem cap and inline-size refitting. Browser checks cover 375px RoleCall/Paper, editing and bidirectional resize. Physical phones, installed apps, real models and packaged behavior remain unverified. HTTP refusals cap bodies at 64 KiB, cancel oversized reads and preserve status; polling pauses in hidden tabs. Backdrop Pick/Change and picture drops use pack staging; collection selection remains separate. Unreadable writing setups retain their saved selection and error beside the picker until another setup or Run Without Preset is chosen.
topics: Prompting presets, guides, note and writing tools
Final Cut passes, Activity and Regex
Take pill, Messenger, reply changes and summary as scene state

children.title: Stage Gallery
children.summary: The Stage wing's Gallery tab ports RoleCall's Image Gallery as a two-column grid of square tiles over the scene's own art: the frozen portrait, the card's extra art and background, the persona's portrait and one pack's pictures, never a link. Tiles use 256 thumbnails and a virtualized window, the panel counts pictures, and the enlarged view offers Download and Use as background, which copies cast art into the scene's pack before setting the backdrop and reports a failed copy without changing it. Generated Received images are left out, and the strip shows no count chip.

children.title: Stage Wardrobe
children.summary: The Stage wing's Wardrobe tab ports RoleCall's WardrobeWingPanel and is shown for every scene, since Bunzai has no beta tier. It hangs the message themes the scene's regex sets carry: display rules whose replacement opens with a style block. An outfit is paired with the preset choice option that carries its name, and its chip writes that choice answer. Unclaimed outfits are loose garments. A standalone dress is worn or hung by switching its set for the scene. The look is the scene's display regex in the sandbox worker. A hung dress stays on the scene's own rack across reloads, fixing a RoleCall flaw.

children.title: Scene theme variants
children.summary: A theme selects one host-built variant for each of six scene surfaces (layout, message, composer, swipes, wings, hud); variants are CSS keyed on the root surface attribute, with markup differing only for version dots, wing labels and the HUD readout. Every control stays present in every variant.

sections.title: The Workbench room (home by default - the IDE)
sections.summary: Workbench owns persistent tabs, follow policy, split view, recents, dirty-close confirmation and drafts. Editors use light baselines, serialized revision-checked patches, conflict choices and bounded history. Lore folders share undo/save ownership; named assets travel with accepted submissions. Complete exports read full entities. Session-granted uploads are revoked on lock or close; pictures are capped at 10 MiB. Measured lists retain focus and selection. Timer autosaves group by five minutes; manual saves keep version boundaries. Character editing defaults to Grid, with a guided quiz; preset groups form a category tree, lorebooks focus one entry, quick replies are ordered messages, and tracker/tool/dice/formula editors share decoded saves. Studio Strip groups identity and save state above compact platform, mode, view and completion controls. View options retains arrangement, Workshop and scale; Desk/Nodes, focus, Save and Export remain reachable. Controls wrap to their container and preserve theme layout locks. Empty or failed benches show a framed room header. Prior storage paths retain their source-review and pending-live-proof limits.

children.title: Editor theme variants
children.summary: editor.frame rearranges eight editors: character, persona, sprite pack, HTML doc, preset, lorebook, regex and quick reply. Each editor declares its sections and hands them to the shared EditorLayout, which renders a two-pane section list, a numbered tabbed menu, a stack of section cards, or one long document with a contents margin. Closed sections stay mounted so unsaved input survives switching, and picking a regex rule or lorebook entry opens its page section. With no pick each editor keeps its own layout, and the character Bento and Playbill choice is disabled while a theme frame is active. editor.fields styles every field drawn through EditorField, except the header name.

children.title: Nodes view
children.summary: Desk and Nodes share open pieces without losing drafts. The canvas has Links, Pipeline and Board layers. Links edit stored references through single-field saves and respect unsaved Desk edits. Pipeline opens presets into blocks for toggling and reordering and wires cast and Lore pass into markers. Feature placement controls appear for placed markers; Feature placements reveals unused controls. Hidden controls do not affect Fit or the minimap. Only actual preset markers receive feature wires; controls do not indicate activity or enable features. Dragging a placement port onto a block places its marker; Delete on its wire switches it off. A Request node previews the forecast or a dry run; board items never export.

sections.title: The Table Read (create by conversation)
sections.summary: The discovered Table Read app is offered beside blank character creation. Cold Read, Deep Dive and Rapid Fire use saved model connections beside an editable canonical card. Accepted answers and manual field ownership persist encrypted. Stop, retry and offline review retain drafts. Rapid Fire starts after preparation and never spends inference on expiry or reload. Explicit Save creates an ordinary character with exact-ID recovery; Workbench opens the result. Temporary browser Studio is unavailable.

sections.title: The Press room (batch export - the staged set prints)
sections.summary: The Press consumes a shell-owned staged queue from Library or its offer rail, preserving staging across app switches. Linked lorebooks ride with characters; preset behaviorRefs and quickReplyRefs ride as regex and quick-reply sets. Riders can be dropped for one run without changing canonical links. Readiness uses the target coverage declaration and identifies lorebook entries that cannot fire. Each run chooses a platform, declares names and skips, and reports each row. Packs print by reference, one picture at a time; unreadable pictures fail their row. One output is delivered bare, while multiple outputs form a ZIP. Installed exports share fresh timestamped Export folders with Kit and the single-piece dialog. Incomplete copies report failure and leave the download available; remote and Browser Studio clients download locally. Each bundle or solo remains a framed panel edged by its deck color.

sections.title: The Agent window (the model, standing on the screen you came from)
sections.summary: A conversation with whatever model the vault holds, carrying the real tool belt. The window owns no provider and no tools: it asks the loopback server, which asks Kit, so there is one vault, one egress ledger and one Gate. Before a write, the Gate opens a host-owned dark-ground alert dialog in the native top layer; the server dispatch loop waits for the person's answer before applying the write. It sees the screen because each app publishes an agentSurface and the mounted app adds what is on it now, joined into a brief that truncates a describe at 300 characters. That snapshot travels through the context both ways, never by importing live-state: every app is bundled separately, so its own import is a second empty copy. The shell publishes a bare snapshot as any app mounts. Replies are drawn from React elements, never from an HTML string. The docked room is one framed panel under a room header showing the model and the screen it stands on; the floating panel keeps its own head.

sections.title: CSS Workshop (catalog-only - assisted CSS authoring)
sections.summary: A catalog-only room for authoring the CSS a card or a host will carry, rather than the CSS this app is built from. It offers starters to begin from, property knobs for the common adjustments, the plain CSS source for anything the knobs do not reach, and a sealed preview showing the result. The output leaves by copy or download for any host, and the room writes no studio state of its own, so nothing here is a piece and nothing needs saving. The preview uses the same seal every untrusted-markup surface in this app uses, which is what lets it show authored CSS without that CSS reaching the application around it. The room header holds only copy, download, clear and tour; the Simple and Advanced switch, Import .css and Undo live in the editor toolbar.

sections.title: Help / Docs (catalog-only - the corpus, in the app)
sections.summary: The committed documentation corpus is a first-class room, read from the same source GitHub serves so the app and repository cannot disagree about a page. It reads docs/generated/docs-index.json rather than crawling the tree; every discovered Markdown page keeps its structural title, summary, and headings in the app. A semantic sidecar enriches that record only when its current receipt independently approves it. Until then, the page remains listed with semantic summary and topics absent, while docs-index:check reports incomplete review status. The reader starts as one mobile article column: Browse and Sections open the shared bottom sheet, which contains keyboard focus, closes on Escape, and restores the trigger. Container breakpoints add the catalog rail at 40rem and the current-page heading rail at 62rem, making the same room adapt correctly inside a phone or split pane without viewport assumptions. The room opens under a Help / Docs header.

sections.title: The Macro Lab (catalog-only - what a macro actually does)
sections.summary: A scratch pad for macro text and the only surface that needs no piece open to be useful. It keeps two answers apart on purpose. Reading is pure and local: each token is broken out against the chosen platform catalog, nested tokens report under their container, and where else does it work asks the translator rather than two catalogs, so a shared name meaning different things is a flagged collision instead of a clean trip. A token invoking no name is called that rather than supported, because isMacroSupported fails lenient by design. Resolving runs the text through the platform real engine as a one-block preset behind a host-only route, needs a local checkout pointed at in Settings or named by an environment variable, and refuses by name when absent. The bible lists every macro with click-to-insert, and the operations table derives from the catalogs with gaps sorted first. The room has its own header and a framed text panel; a dot marks platforms whose engine is installed.

sections.title: HTML View (catalog-only - a drawing at full size)
sections.summary: A catalog-only app that draws one htmldoc piece as a whole tab. It is reached three ways: opened by id from the Library, handed a piece by another surface, or handed the raw text of a fenced html block from an agent reply. A piece travels by ID and is re-read from the studio, so the tab shows what the drawing says now; only an unsaved reply is carried whole, and the room says so rather than showing an empty frame. Everything drawn passes through SealedHtmlPreview, the component behind the transcript preview and the Workbench editor pane too, so one boundary serves three sizes with nothing to drift. The tab and the editor pane fill their room while the transcript keeps the inline ceiling, and either goes fullscreen, natively where allowed and as an overlay where not. All CSS renders, head styles included. JavaScript never runs, no remote image or webfont loads, and form controls are stripped, since the same component draws untrusted card backdrops. The header title is the drawing's name.

sections.title: Settings (drop-in sections)
sections.summary: Settings derives its sections from modules. Extensions owns package review, operation and appearance grants, lifecycle controls, private-data usage, redacted receipts and host-rendered contributions. Effect requests use expiring host-owned tickets and shared controls rather than guest HTML or CSS. Appearance owns theme selection, accents and stage lights; Models shares the provider vault with Kit. Studio, Workbench, Connections, Security, Backups, Memory and Summaries, Remote access, Updates and About remain separate sections. Protected pages preserve their lock state.
topics: Spotify Client ID and loopback sign-in
Studio home deck targets and engine checkouts

children.title: Settings theme variants
children.summary: Settings theme variants restyle the page body, rows and segmented control through data-sx hooks. They no longer touch the rail of acts, which belongs to the room. Stylesheets live under the settings variants folder.

sections.title: Shared components (`src/ui/_shared/` and `src/ui/components/`)
sections.summary: Every clickable control is a named part of the button family in src/ui/components/button (Button, IconButton, Segmented, Tabs, DocTab, Chip, ListRow, MenuItem, Disclosure, Tile, Card, Dot, Toggle, InlineValue, Scrim), each tagged with data-control (and data-kind where it has kinds) as theme hooks; lint blocks raw buttons and the style guard blocks button CSS elsewhere. Shared visual controls are extracted once for setup, settings, and future editors. SwatchRow exposes the house palette as quick choices and optionally opens PaintPicker for a custom solid color. ColorPicker provides a branded saturation/value square, hue strip, and hex input while retaining HSV internally to avoid grayscale-state loss. Pure color math normalizes and converts values fail-closed and shares pointer fractions across color and gradient controls. The Paint model is a validated discriminated union for solid, linear, and radial output; gradients require at least two valid stops. PaintPicker composes color editing, stop add/drag/remove, angle adjustment, and curved previews behind allowed-mode gates. Solid accent use is live; tested gradient editing awaits its first entity or pack background consumer.

children.title: House style (Premiere)
children.summary: Every room wears a room header with a gold kicker, a display-face title, one lede line and right-aligned actions. Groups sit in a single framed panel with an offset shadow and an optional piece-kind deck edge; a panel nested inside another flattens to its colored top edge, so frames never nest. The Workbench editor head adds a kind kicker and deck color. Colors come from the theme's brand, action and select roles, so rooms follow the user's accent. Monospace is reserved for code, ids and numbers, and the core UI font fallback is Atkinson Hyperlegible.

children.title: Control variants (`ui.controls`)
children.summary: ui.controls is a global variant painted once into the head by the shell; it sets the button family offset and frame through the data-control hook on Button and IconButton, field frames and the focus ring, and every element rule excludes .host-protected. variant-css-check.ts holds the proofs each variant owes. The app.room surface rearranges the setup wizard, Press, Agent room and CSS Workshop per theme, and ui.empty frames every element marked data-empty, including the workbench empty room.

sections.title: Approved jewel Library and Scenes
sections.summary: Library and Scenes adopt the approved black surfaces, gilded rules and jewel accents; the other page proposals remain awaiting approval. Lorebooks without artwork get stable compositions from 60 transparent semantic PNG ornaments and ten painterly paper layers. Design book cover uses the existing lorebook menu to edit layers and cover title or restore original artwork. These are local Studio presentation preferences, separate from canonical and escrowed content, and are not baked into exports; imported artwork is retained by default. The catalog is derived from asset folders. Scenes persists Pictures or List through scenes.view. Recent lists have This Week and Earlier headings while message-ranked lists retain their ordering without date groups. Both layouts share the measured virtualizer, frozen art, selection and context menus; narrow rows retain time, take count, active take and a visible menu. The overview includes a Continue hero with real tail preview and a measured Fan Favorites shelf ordered by star time.

sections.title: Security
sections.summary: Authenticated server routes enforce path and request boundaries; imported Lua/regex remain sealed data until user-invoked isolated test benches. Upload staging bounds formats, bytes, grant count and lifetime; inert SVG/CSS rules reject active payloads. Lock or close aborts active uploads and revokes grants. Library, mentions, status and recents share PieceStore; exact summary identity and lock lifetimes fence delayed metadata and recovery. These integrated paths are source-reviewed, with focused fixture results recorded in delivery evidence and live proof pending.

children.title: Additional chat layouts from VAUDEVILLE
children.summary: scenes.chatLayout selects Full Chat, Familiar, Basic, Desktop 98, Messenger, Immersive, Letters, Notebook, or Storybook through the shared layout options. Every layout keeps the existing transcript, composer, turn, and edit owners. Desktop 98 reuses existing wing bodies in temporary movable windows; the paper layouts adapt their reading pages to narrow panes. Theme packages do not replace the layout shells, and Messenger avatars retain their fixed crop.
